title: Projectile Motion with Drag & Undo/Redo
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that simulates projectile motion with air drag, featuring undo/redo functionality. Load the 3D model 'Corset.glb' using GLTFLoader from a CDN as the projectile.

SCENE SETUP:
- Use a perspective camera at position (0, 10, 30) looking at the origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.5) and a directional light at (10, 20, 10) with intensity 1.0.
- Create a large green ground plane (100x100) at y=0 using MeshStandardMaterial.
- Add a grid helper (100 divisions) on the ground for visual reference.
- Load 'Corset.glb' using GLTFLoader (use CDN: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/examples/jsm/loaders/GLTFLoader.js). Scale the model to (3, 3, 3) so it is visible. This is the projectile.
- Place the projectile initially at position (-30, 0.5, 0) on the ground.
- Add a small red sphere (radius 0.5) at position (20, 0.5, 0) as the target marker.

PHYSICS:
- Implement projectile motion with quadratic air drag: F_drag = -0.5 * Cd * rho * A * |v| * v
- Use parameters: Cd=0.47, rho=1.225 (air density), A=0.1 (cross-section area), mass=1.0 kg, gravity=9.81 m/s².
- Use Euler integration with dt = 1/60.
- The projectile launches from its current position with configurable launch angle and initial speed.
- When the projectile hits the ground (y <= 0), stop the simulation and record the landing position.

USER INTERACTIONS:
- A 'Launch' button (id='launchBtn') fires the projectile with current angle and speed settings.
- An angle slider (id='angleSlider', range 10-80, default 45) with a label showing the value (id='angleLabel').
- A speed slider (id='speedSlider', range 5-40, default 20) with a label showing the value (id='speedLabel').
- A 'Reset' button (id='resetBtn') returns the projectile to start position (-30, 0.5, 0) and clears trajectory.
- An 'Undo' button (id='undoBtn') reverts to the previous launch state (position, trajectory, landed status).
- A 'Redo' button (id='redoBtn') re-applies the undone launch.
- Draw a trajectory trail using THREE.Line with yellow color showing the projectile path.
- Press 'Space' key to also trigger launch (same as clicking Launch button).

STATE MANAGEMENT:
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- projectileX, projectileY, projectileZ: current projectile position
- velocityX, velocityY, velocityZ: current velocity components
- isFlying: boolean, true while projectile is in the air
- hasLanded: boolean, true once projectile touches ground after launch
- launchAngle: current angle in degrees
- launchSpeed: current initial speed
- launchCount: total number of launches performed
- undoStackSize: number of states available to undo
- redoStackSize: number of states available to redo
- trailPointCount: number of points in the current trajectory trail
- distanceToTarget: distance from projectile to target marker (red sphere at 20,0.5,0)
- dragEnabled: always true (drag is always on)
- maxHeight: maximum Y reached during current/last flight

HUD:
- Display current position (x, y rounded to 1 decimal) in a div (id='positionHUD') at top-left.
- Display launch count in a div (id='launchCountHUD').
- Display max height in a div (id='maxHeightHUD').
- All controls in a panel (id='controlPanel') at bottom of screen.

UNDO/REDO LOGIC:
- Each completed launch (projectile has landed) pushes a snapshot to the undo stack containing: landing position, trajectory points, maxHeight, launchAngle, launchSpeed.
- Clicking Undo pops the last snapshot, restores the projectile to start, clears the trail, and pushes the snapshot to the redo stack.
- Clicking Redo pops from redo stack and restores that launch result (shows trail, projectile at landing spot, hasLanded=true).
- A new launch clears the redo stack.
- Undo/Redo buttons should be disabled (grayed out) when their respective stacks are empty.
physics_constraints: Projectile motion with quadratic drag: F_drag = -0.5 * 0.47 * 1.225 * 0.1 * |v| * v_component. Gravity = 9.81 m/s² downward. Euler integration at dt=1/60. Projectile stops when y <= 0. Mass = 1.0 kg. Launch direction is in the XY plane (positive X forward, positive Y up).
